en: Now, as always, of course, you know the
game. All the details for executing it are
in that README,
and you will need that OpenAI API key, of
course.
So with that setup, we can run
this agent.py file
and then ask it,
look up the
order by Alex and refund it.
It should be able to do that. We have
orders.json here, we have an Alex, we have
only one Alex in there. It should find this
order. That order is below our threshold, so
it should be able to automatically refund
it.
So if I send that to the
model, it's reading orders.json
and you see it simulated the refund. It was
successful because it was below that
threshold.
Now if I run it again, refund the order by
Sam, it should not be able to do that
automatically because that amount is higher
than $10 and indeed therefore it's asking
me.
And here I
can choose
no or just hit enter and then this is
denied.
So I couldn't refund.
If I try this again,
copying this message,
refund the order by Sam,
it of course again looks up the data. If I
now enter Y or yes, both works,
it simulates that refund and the model gets
the information that the refund was issued.
And that shows us how we can handle a human
in the loop, how we can simply execute tool
calls conditionally, and how we can put
logic into a sandbox or put tool calls into
a sandbox. And please note that these are
all things the model can't work around or
the agent can't work around because our
logic for the sandbox and also our logic for
asking for approval is hardcoded in those
tools.
If we would just instruct the agent to, for
example, ask for approval
before issuing
refunds greater than $10,
we would have to hope that it does that in
the right way. The same if we would tell it,
don't work outside of sandbox. We could do
that and most likely it will adhere to that,
but it's not a hard rule.
That's why we wanna encode such logic
in our code so that the model can't work
around it because it doesn't control that
code. Now obviously, as mentioned before, if
you had a more versatile
Bash tool that would allow the model, the
agent in the end, to write and execute its
own programs,
things could change because it could write
its own script that can break out of the
sandbox. But with basic tools like read file
and write file, we have a secure mechanism
for enclosing or capturing the agent in a
certain path, for example.
If you have more complex requirements, if
you need to put an entire agent into a
sandbox or anything like that, you can of
course also look into dedicated tools and
solutions like Docker
or one of the many sandbox providers or
sandbox frameworks, libraries you could say,
like AgentOS.
But the core idea is always the same. You
wanna control via your code what happens for
which tools.
